points.title: The main rule
points.must: Every data flow must start or end at a process — data is stored, read or passed on only by a process.

points.title: Not allowed flows
points.must: Entity→entity, entity→store (or store→entity), store→store, each with the reason; how to fix by adding a process.

points.title: Rules for processes
points.must: At least one input and one output; verb + noun name; numbers only identify, they do not show order.

points.title: Rules for stores and flows
points.must: Each store written and read by processes; every flow labelled with a noun; one direction per arrow; no decisions or loops.

points.title: Black hole and miracle
points.must: Black hole: inputs but no output; miracle: outputs but no input; each with an example.

points.title: Grey hole
points.must: Outputs cannot be produced from the inputs (e.g. total calculated from a name only).

points.title: Finding errors (worked example)
points.must: Gym example or similar: illegal flows identified with the reason and the correction.

points.title: Steps to draw a level-1 DFD
points.must: Underline entities; verbs → processes; kept data → stores; list inputs/outputs of each process; draw with named arrows; check rules and balance.

points.title: Pizza shop level-1 DFD
points.must: Entities Customer, Bank, Kitchen; processes Take order, Process payment, Send order to kitchen; stores Menu, Orders; named flows.

points.title: Checking a DFD
points.must: Each process has input and output; each store written and read; no illegal flows; all flows labelled; balanced.

points.title: DFD vs flowchart vs ERD
points.must: Comparison: data movement vs sequence and decisions vs entities and relationships; what each is used for.

points.title: Advantages and limitations
points.must: Advantages: simple, client can check, whole system on one page; limitations: no order, no algorithms, many levels for big systems.
